item.title: Nintendo has announced Pikmin 4: Switch 2 Edition, an enhanced version of the brilliant real-time strategy game with new content and upgraded visuals.
item.description:
Nintendo has announced Pikmin 4: Switch 2 Edition, an enhanced version of the brilliant real-time strategy game with new content and upgraded visuals launching on November 12.
You can use voice commands to chat and move Oatchi. A new mode, Dandori Academy, will see you racing against the clock to complete treasure hunts before time runs out. This offering is all about high scores, with three difficulty options and weekly challenges every Friday, Saturday and Sunday. 72 Dandori Academy stages will be available over time.
The brilliant Pikmin 4 originally launched for the original Switch back in July 2023, and was greeted by a warm response from fans and critics alike. Still, the game never received any additional post-launch content, even though it sold well in comparison to its predecessors (particularly in Japan, where Pikmin 4 beat the launch sales of the series' previous three installments combined).
Once again, Pikmin 4 follows a team of explorers setting foot on an alien world (that's actually Earth), aided by a horde of helpful creatures (that's your Pikmin). This fourth major game adds indoor and night-time gameplay, as well as a useful dog-like companion (named Oatchi) who smoothes over some of the series' fussier gameplay.
In short, Pikmin 4 revives and enhances the series' best features to provide the best and most complete-feeling Pikmin game to date, with the return of Pikmin 2's dungeon-like caves and the inclusion of every major Pikmin species all very welcome. It's also a very generous game already in terms of content, with unlockable side-modes and a fun story campaign, that will now become more generous still.
Catch up on all of the big announcements in our roundup of everything announced in today's Nintendo Direct broadcast, as well as everything announced in The Legend of Zelda Nintendo Direct that aired yesterday.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Capcom has announced a Monster Hunter Wilds Nintendo Switch 2 release date of December 4, 2026.
item.description:
Capcom has announced a Monster Hunter Wilds Nintendo Switch 2 release date of December 4, 2026.
The latest entry in the publisher’s monster-hunting series kicked off today’s September 2026 Nintendo Direct. Additional details about the release include confirmation that the Switch 2 version of Monster Hunter Wilds will come with local play and all previous title updates.
Capcom announced earlier this year that Monster Hunter Wilds was Switch 2 bound but declined to share a specific release date. It led some to believe we may have to wait until next year to get our hands on the game, making today's December announcement a nice surprise.
"Venture into the Forbidden Lands to track and hunt massive monsters, craft gear, and uncover the mysteries of an ever-changing world," Nintendo said. "Whether playing at home or on the go, hunters can team up locally via wireless play or join friends online with full cross-platform multiplayer support. All Title Update content is included, such as the Grand Hub, fan-favorite monsters like Mizutsune and Lagiacrus, the FINAL FANTASY XIV Online collaboration, and more. Monster Hunter Wilds launches for Nintendo Switch 2 on Dec. 4."
Nintendo has also confirmed that Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance will come to Switch 2 at some point in 2027. The expansion is expected to come to PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S at some point next year, too, though it's unclear if it will receive a simultaneous launch across all platforms.
A Switch 2 port for Monster Hunter Wilds is something fans have been looking forward to for a while. Capcom launched its latest installment all the way back in February 2025, meaning Nintendo fans will be fast approaching the game's second anniversary by the time it actually launches for the hybrid sequel console. It's hard to say if the wait will have been worth it, but those who have spent the last few months hoping to see it arrive sooner rather than later will surely be happy to see it out so soon.
IGN gave Monster Hunter Wilds an 8/10 review. At the time we said it "continues to smooth off the rougher corners of the series in smart ways, making for some extremely fun fights but also lacking any real challenge."
In case you forgot, this is Nintendo’s second Direct of the week. For everything announced during yesterday’s Zelda Direct, click here. For everything announced during today’s Direct, click here.
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: Xiri: Oasis Cities, a survival-focused, high-tech, future-set city-builder, has been announced for PC. Your desert oasis (hence the name) will face "natural disasters, cyber warfare, and fragile political alliances between neighboring settlements," according to the small indie team behind the project.
item.description:
Xiri: Oasis Cities, a survival-focused, high-tech, future-set city-builder, has been announced for PC. Your desert oasis (hence the name) will face "natural disasters, cyber warfare, and fragile political alliances between neighboring settlements," according to the small indie team behind the project.
As you build and manage your city, you'll have to manage an evolving population that includes humans, androids, and drones. Also, if you've ever wanted to engage in some good old-fashioned industrial espionage, this might be the game for you, as things are ruthless in Xiri's megacorp-run future. The inter-corporate shenanigans extend beyond that, too, as you'll "launch cyberattacks against rival infrastructure, manage loyalty levels, negotiate loans, detect spies, and manipulate economic conditions."
Check out the first screenshots in the gallery above and the announcement trailer at the top of this page. You can also wishlist Xiri: Oasis Cities on Steam if you're interested.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: What We Do in the Shadows' Matt Berry voices an IKEA Kallax bookcase in a free official Creation for The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim.
item.description:
What We Do in the Shadows' Matt Berry voices an IKEA Kallax bookcase in a free official Creation for The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim.
The infamous IKEA storage unit will become a fully-fledged in-game companion, Kallax Storageborn, able to carry your items and prevent you becoming easily over-encumbered. You'll even be able to summon him with a custom Dragon Shout (AYE-KEY-YAH). Yes, IKEA.
Why is Berry being roped in to lend his baritone boom to a bookcase? Well, this is an officially-licensed IKEA collaboration that plays on the infamous annoyance of being over-encumbered within the game.
But there's seemingly more here than just a simple joke. Not only have Berry's talents been secured, but developer Kinggath Creations has crafted a full quest with two new IKEA-themed dungeons, and a boss fight against the Clutter Golem. Need help assembling your inventory? You'll also be able to wield the Dwemer Allen Key weapon, wear the Meatball Helmet, and gobble meatball food items.
"At IKEA, we believe in creating a better everyday life for the many people — and why shouldn't that include their digital lives?" said IKEA exec Kemi Anthony. "Skyrim possesses one of the largest modding communities in gaming, and we saw a space where our expertise in functional storage could make a real difference in this fantasy world.
"Matt Berry's distinctive, legendary voice brings theatrics, booming authority and charm to the new Creation. In bringing Kallax to life we hope to not only make a meaningful difference for Skyrim players but doing so with a touch of added IKEA playfulness to delight gamers who've long been bogged down by too much stuff."
This isn't Berry's first video game credit, of course. You can hear his dulcet tones right now in LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight as Bane, or in the celebrated 2024 British indie adventure Thank Goodness You're Here!
It's a busy time for Berry, who is due to appear next year in both Sonic the Hedgehog 4 and A Minecraft Movie Squared. This year, he'll appear as The Fish in a new Bill Hader-starring adaptation of The Cat in the Hat.
The IKEA Kallax Storageborn add-on Creation will be available to download for free via Bethesda Game Studios in-game Creations menu from today, September 9.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: No Man’s Sky developer Hello Games has continued the relentless pace of updates for the space game, this time releasing a 10th anniversary patch called Cosmos.
item.description:
No Man’s Sky developer Hello Games has continued the relentless pace of updates for the space game, this time releasing a 10th anniversary patch called Cosmos.
Hello Games chief Sean Murray said Cosmos is one of No Man Sky’s “biggest and craziest” updates ever, as it actually updates space.
“No Man’s Sky is often referred to as ‘a Space Game,’ it’s a huge part of our game, but we’ve never really updated space since release,” Murray said. “In most sci-fi games, space is just an empty void. With Cosmos we wondered - can we make space feel truly alive? And could we make space feel more like home? What if you could own a Space Station? If you could build star bases, and create alliances with other players.”
Additions include a Star Map, huge space hulks, new space outposts, bio-wrecks, asteroid belts, free-floating orbital bases, space station ownership (one of the most requested features since launch), alliances, and — finally — the ability to actually reach the star at the center of players’ own star system.
Hello Games has launched an expedition alongside the Cosmos update, called Our Journey Continues! It includes milestones that represent one of the 40 major updates since No Man’s Sky launched in 2016. “It is like a museum of each update, unlocking the features of each update as we added them, along with a spacelog of interesting facts and developers commentary for each update,” Murray explained. “It’s been a real joy to revisit some of those moments for us.”

item.title: Hot on the heels of yesterday’s The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct, we have a brand new Nintendo Direct — and IGN will be reporting all the news live right here.
item.description:
Nintendo Direct September 2026 is over, and we have all the announcements right here.
Highlights included the reveal of Metroid Ravenous, a new 2D, side-scrolling Metroid game, a new Kirby game called Kirby and the World Beyond, and a free update for Mario Kart world Tour.
But there were a number of games that were conspicuous by their absence. Perhaps the biggest offender here is FromSoftware's Switch 2 exclusive The Duskbloods, which fans had hoped would get a release date during the Nintendo Direct. This is a game currently down for release in 2026, so Nintendo is running out of time to either announce a release date or delay it into 2027.
We didn't see any more of the Ocarina of Time remake, although that was expected after yesterday's reveal, nor did Nintendo tease the next 3D Mario game, which was always something of a pipe dream. But we do now have a clearer idea of what's coming to Switch 2 for the rest of 2026 and into next year. So, what do you think? Let us know in the comments. And if you need a catchup, all the announcements are rounded up below.
Nintendo direct September 2026 ended with a brand new Kirby game, revealed new Mario Kart World DLC, and Metroid Ravenous, among other things. Let us know what you thought of the show in the comments!
Nintendo Direct ended with the announcement of a brand new Kirby Game: Kirby and the World Beyond. It's due out on Switch 2 spring 2027. This latest 3D adventure lets you freely explore using Kirby's copy abilities. Next year marks Kirby's 35th anniversary, and Nintendo said to look out for fresh announcements for the series.
"A new 3D adventure is on the horizon for Kirby!" Nintendo said. "Freely explore an expansive world and put Kirby’s Copy Abilities to creative use as you uncover what awaits in Kirby and the World Beyond. The game is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 in spring 2027, which also marks the Kirby series’ 35th anniversary."
Atlus showed up at Nintendo Direct to confirm Persona 4 Revival and Persona 6 are coming to Nintendo Switch 2! Persona 4 Revival launches on Nintendo Switch 2 on May 20, 2027. Persona 6 doesn't have a release window yet.
Featuring a visually enhanced version of the original Danganronpa 2: Goodbye Despair scenario alongside a brand new story with the same setting and characters, Danganronpa 2x2 will see players investigate an entirely new set of victims, culprits, and tricks. Danganronpa 2x2 launches for Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch on January 14, 2027.
The latest entry in the Yo-kai Watch series evolves the adventures of Yo-kai Watch 2: Bony Spirits, Fleshy Souls and Psychic Specters with enhanced graphics and new content on Nintendo Switch 2. Join Nate as he befriends a wide variety of Yo-kai and embarks on the mysterious adventures that define the series. Along with new story content, players may even encounter some new Yo-kai. Additional details will be shared in the future.
A new semester begins as Yu-Gi-Oh! GX TAG FORCE 3 is reborn with modern visuals, enhanced Dueling and nostalgic cards from the Yu-Gi-Oh! GX anime era. Featuring content previously unreleased in the Americas, Yu-Gi-Oh! TAG FORCE GX launches for Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch on Feb. 16, 2027. Pre-orders begin later today on Nintendo eShop and include four in-game items for the Yu-Gi-Oh! MASTER DUEL game. Physical versions include three Yu-Gi-Oh! TRADING CARD GAME cards.
During today’s Nintendo Direct, Square Enix revealed a 3D remake of 1995 RPG, Romancing SaGa 3: Destinies United. Destinies United has 3D graphics, fully voiced cutscenes, overhauls combat and other mechanics, adds selectable difficulty levels and other new features. Romancing SaGa 3: Destinies United releases on Nintendo Switch 2, Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and PC via Steam on February 16, 2027.
Nintendo Direct announced Metal Slug Ultimate Collection, which includes 10 classic Metal Slug games. There's online multiplayer, online leaderboards, and a gallery of artwork and music from across the series. Combat School Mode returns with expanded content, alongside the long-lost location test version of Metal Slug Metal Slug Ultimate Collection launches for Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch in 2027.
JRPG Eternal Anima launches on Switch 2 on March 4, 2027. It's from Marvelous Europe, and is developed by director Katsuhisa Higuchi, story concept writer Keisuke Makino, and scenario writer Kazushige Nojima. This is the game originally teased under the working title “PROJECT LIFE is RPG” in 2023. Marvelous said Eternal Anima "evokes the spirit of late 1990s and early 2000s JRPGs, while featuring an ambitious time-travelling narrative, modern visuals, and strategic twists on traditional turn-based gameplay." The debut trailer is below.
Mega Man: Dual Override got a new trailer and confirmation of amiibo figures. It's due out spring 2027. Here's the official word from Nintendo:
Nintendo announced a free Mario Kart World update, which adds classic courses from Super Mario Kart such as Choco Island, Vanilla Lake, and Ghost Valley. The free update adds 10 new courses, and two new routes to Knockout Tour. The 1.8.0 update for Mario Kart World launches later today! Here's the official blurb from Nintendo:
A free update for Mario Kart World launches later today!Play 10 classic courses from Super Mario Kart in VS Race mode and two new Knockout tour routes. #NintendoDirectGet the update: https://t.co/K9I0I75Mhh pic.twitter.com/1FIL2jzzQY
Here's a big one! Nintendo announced a new 2D Metroid game called Metroid Ravenous. The trailer revealed fast-paced action, boss fights, and dramatic cutscenes. "It's eat or be eaten," Samus declares. It's due out January 28, 2027. There are new amiibo figures and a Metroid Ravenous Nintendo Switch 2 Special Edition also due out then.
Here's the official blurb from Nintendo:
As expected, Direct gave us a new look at Nintendo Switch Sports Resort. It's due out on Switch 2 on October 22. Here's the official blurb:
Get moving on Wuhu Island! Nintendo Switch Sports Resort launches exclusively for Nintendo Switch 2 on Oct 22. #NintendoDirectPre-order today: https://t.co/W21rIC7kUD pic.twitter.com/5R1hIswLD9
Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis hits Switch 2 on February 12, 2027. New trailer is below.
Adventure beyond legend. Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 on Feb 12! Pre-orders start later today. #NintendoDirect @PlayTombRaider pic.twitter.com/yZjBeBJizH
Resident Evil 2 Deluxe Edition, Resident Evil 3, and Resident Evil 4 Gold Edition launch on the Switch 2 on October 16, 2026. Preorders begin later today.
Cairn launches on Switch 2 early next year. A free demo goes live on the eShop later today. "As pro climber Aava, set out to conquer the legendary Mount Kami in this acclaimed climbing simulation with a deeply human story about overcoming impossible odds," Nintendo said. "Climb anywhere, plan your route carefully and manage resources throughout the expedition. The whole mountain is yours to explore as you uncover mysteries and push beyond your limits in pursuit of absolute freedom. A free demo will be available later today on Nintendo eShop, ahead of the game’s Nintendo Switch 2 launch early next year."
New Kirby Air Riders amiibo launches November 12 with the release of Sword Kirby & Dragoon and Noir Dedede & Hydra. That completes the Kirby Air Riders lineup, Nintendo said. An upcoming Kirby Air Riders in-game event will also offer rewards and refresh the look of the main menu and Paddock.
New amiibo figures are riding in to complete the Kirby Air Riders lineup! Sword Kirby & Dragoon as well as Noir Dedede & Hydra will be available on Nov 12. #NintendoDirect pic.twitter.com/ykiQTNjUFZ
LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight launches on Switch 2 on September 18.
Ondeh Ondeh Kaya's Tasty Tale from Bandai Namco is due out on Switch 2 next year. It's described as "a charming rhythm and puzzle action-adventure" developed by Metronomik, "inviting players to embark on a magical journey inspired by the vibrant cultures of Southeast Asia." The game combines action-packed gameplay with exploration and clever puzzles incorporating the region’s rich heritage in music, cuisine and other beloved cultural elements, even taking the name of the traditional sweet snack, ondeh ondeh, into its title.
Stage Fright is coming to Switch and Switch 2 next year. It's from Overcooked! developer Ghost Town Games Ltd, and is published by No Man's Sky studio Hello Games.
We got a new trailer for Xenoblade Chronicles 3 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition, which launches December 3, 2026.
Take down waves of enemies in a new battle mode and team up with a newly-added hero, Shimmer, in #XenobladeChronicles3 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition,launching Dec 3. #NintendoDirectPre-order today: https://t.co/hLMjqrIL9X pic.twitter.com/WZ2AUqjmDh
Nintendo Direct revealed a creepy supernatural game from Silent Hill remake developer Bloober Team. It's playable exclusively in Switch 2 handheld mode, and comes out at some point in 2027. Here's the official blurb:
Nintendo revealed Pikmin 4 Nintendo Switch 2 Edition during the Direct. You can use your voice to order Oatchi about, and there's a new mode called Dandori Academy in which you can take on challenges. You can take exams each week, with 72 stages released over time. It's due out November 12, 2026, and preorders begin later today on the eShop.
Professor Layton and The New World of Steam got a new trailer at Nintendo Direct. It's due out December 10, 2026!
As expected, Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave got a new trailer, showing off the upcoming Switch 2 game. It's due out September 17.
Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 Royal Edition launches on Nintendo Switch 2 next year.
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered launches on Nintendo Switch 2 on September 29. The Songs of the Past paid expansion also hits Switch 2 next year.
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered is coming to Nintendo Switch 2! Embark on the Path when it releases Sept 29. #NintendoDirect @thewitcherOwners of the Nintendo Switch version receive the game for free! Pre-order now: https://t.co/yOWEKjGqQx pic.twitter.com/0dAX3mC4eZ
Star Fox is getting a free update to add new stages on September 29. Meanwhile, Star Fox Adventures launches on Nintendo GameCube - Nintendo Classics later today!
A new update is coming to Star Fox on Sept 29. Join the fray with up to four players locally in Battle Mode with three new stages! #NintendoDirectLearn more: https://t.co/aHTsHOEl4g pic.twitter.com/jp21z0IPg9
Star Fox Adventures is landing on Nintendo GameCube – Nintendo Classics later today!Alongside his pal Tricky, Fox explores a planet populated by dinosaurs, but who knows what they might uncover? #NintendoDirect pic.twitter.com/iie3IPeKlT
In Part 2 of the Pokémon Pokopia Expansion Pass paid DLC, players can dress up Ditto and other Pokémon appearing in Pokémon Pokopia in a range of accessories. These include items such as cool sunglasses, classy bow ties, and even items which allow Ditto to match other Pokémon, such as a Sylveon ribbon. Part 2 is due out later this year.
Get stylish with accessories in Part 2 of the Pokémon Pokopia Expansion Pass paid DLC, releasing later this year! #NintendoDirectLearn more: https://t.co/E3KjpukNrq pic.twitter.com/HST4OWXKJk
Steam mega hit Meccha Chameleon hits Switch later today!
Paint yourself to blend in and trick the seekers. Can you stay hidden? 🎨🦎 MECCHA CHAMELEON is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 later today! #NintendoDirect @lemorion1224 pic.twitter.com/3rIxa2IVNQ
Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity Definitive Edition is coming to Nintendo Switch 2! Expect better visuals and more enemies on-screen. There's also a new harder difficulty called Calamity Mode. If you have the Switch version, you can get a discount on the digital release. It's due out February 25, 2027.
Here's Nintendo's note on the game:
Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity – Definitive Edition comes to Nintendo Switch 2 on Feb 25. #NintendoDirect pic.twitter.com/mJagAUub4C
The Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy ends with Revelation, which is also coming to Switch 2. It's due out on April 8, 2027. Preorders begin later today on the eShop. Meanwhile, Crisis Core –Final Fantasy VII– Reunion, the HD remastered Final Fantasy VII prequel, launches later today on the Nintendo eShop.
Nintendo Direct September 2026 kicked off with a new look at Monster Hunter Wilds on Switch 2. Capcom's hugely popular action adventure hits Switch 2 with local play support and all the updates released so far. It's due out December 4, 2026. The expansion, Ascendance, is also coming to Monster Hunter Wilds on Switch 2 at some point in 2027.
We're 30 minutes away from Nintendo Direct start time. Let us know your predictions in the comments below!
Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: An Anthropic safety researcher has said there is a greater than 10% chance that AI “could kill all humans” within the next decade, and admitted there is no coordinated plan to prevent it from happening.
item.description:
An Anthropic safety researcher has said there is a greater than 10% chance that AI “could kill all humans” within the next decade, and admitted there is no coordinated plan to prevent it from happening.
U.S. company Anthropic, headed up by Dario Amodei, develops the Large Language Model (LLM) Claude and conducts AI research. Yesterday, one of the company’s researchers, Jacob Coxon, announced his resignation on X / Twitter, accusing both ChatGPT maker OpenAI and Anthropic of “racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.”
“Neither company is acting responsible,” Coxon, who previously worked at OpenAI, said. “Do not underestimate the power of this technology. These will soon be superhuman systems that can hack anything, revolutionize any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources,” he continued. “We have all witnessed the progress in each of these domains, and progress is not slowing.
“The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade. This is not a marketing stunt. If anything, many executives and senior researchers will couch their phrasing in the press to sound sensible — but I hear the same people express fear privately. No other human activity poses this level of danger.”
Coxon said that staff at OpenAI, headed up by Sam Altman, “have not deeply internalized the civilizational stakes,” which is why work to rapidly improve its AI models continues despite the risks. “At Anthropic, the stakes are well-understood, but they are locked in a race to get there first," he insisted. “They believe no one else will act responsibly, so they must do it themselves, despite the risk.”
“Accepting this race and entering the ‘endgame’ is a hubristic gamble that should not be launched from a private company’s Slack. Attempting to speedrun alignment should require extraordinary confidence that there are no better trajectories available.”
Coxon went on to say he was optimistic about the potential for coordination, but doubted AI companies were on track to prevent a global race, “which may require costly actions such as a temporary ban on improving model capabilities.”
He ended his statement by urging AI lab researchers to consider what they were doing. “Do you want to kick off a superintelligent RL run without a rigorous understanding of its mind?” he asked. “Should you put your head down because ‘it’s happening anyway’ - or take this moment to call for different conditions?”
Coxon’s statement has sent shockwaves throughout social media, sparking alarm and a string of mainstream headlines. But then it was backed up by Evan Hubinger, Anthropic’s ‘Alignment Science’ lead, who added an even starker warning.
“Jacob is correct here — we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans!” he said. “I personally think it is >10% within the next decade. I believe Anthropic is trying its best, but we do not yet have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence and are not clearly on track to.”
Remarkably, Hubinger pointed to Anthropic’s latest Risk Report, in which the company said it believes the risk from present models is “low,” rather than suggest a pause that might help prevent the extinction of humankind. “What I am worried about is superintelligence arising from recursive self-improvement, as we have said is happening faster than we thought,” he added.
The comments come after the Financial Times reported that Anthropic withheld its latest model from the UK's AI Safety Institute, one of the leading bodies in the world for assessing AI risk.
This summer has seen a number of worrying developments that show how AI has become hard to control, even by those who create it. OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta have all disclosed hacks carried out by their autonomous AI agents. OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki recently called for "extreme caution" over AI progress, warning more intervention may be needed to ensure "humans remain in control of the future.”
However, the U.S. government has shown no sign of stepping in to force restrictions upon or even suggest a slowing down of AI development. In fact, quite the opposite. Earlier this month, the Trump administration backed OpenAI in ⁠a lawsuit against the New York Times, arguing in favor of the use of copyrighted writing to train artificial intelligence. “The United States has a strong interest in continuing to develop a robust and competitive artificial intelligence industry that sets the standard for the practice and procedure of AI use globally… As such, it is critical for the United States to ‘retain global leadership in artificial intelligence,'” the government's brief said, referencing an executive order President Donald Trump signed last year.
Meanwhile, despite dire warnings coming from staff at Anthropic and OpenAI, neither company seems willing to pull the plug. Coxon and Hubinger’s statements have sparked extreme concern across social media, with some expressing disbelief that work to improve AI is continuing even with such significant risk.
“Hey! Here’s a novel idea… could we just f***ing not kill ourselves due to an insatiable appetite for power and money?” one person said. “Crazy take: maybe you shouldn’t be allowed to gamble with our lives?” another added. “If I literally claimed that there was a 10% chance that I was building something that would kill people, the FBI would have me arrested. How are you not in jail?” another asked.
Photo Illustration by Dominika Zarzycka/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images.

item.title: Achievements for various upcoming games have been made public as part of a significant Steam leak.
item.description:
Achievements for various upcoming games have been made public as part of a significant Steam leak.
Spoiler-filled achievements for Persona 6 and Kingdom Hearts 4, among many others, appeared on achievement tracking website Exophase. In the case of Kingdom Hearts 4, the achievements reveal unannounced worlds. The Persona 6 achievements hint at plot points.
Little is known about Persona 6, which was announced during June’s Xbox Games Showcase with the teaser, below.
We do know it's a day-one Game Pass title, though, and that it is due out on Xbox Series X and S, PlayStation 5 and PC via Steam. Here’s the official blurb:
Square Enix has announced just one Kingdom Hearts 4 world so far: Coco. Last month, Kingdom Hearts 4 co-director Tai Yasue and series creator Tetsuya Nomura assured fans that it is a "100% thing" the game will not be delayed past its late 2027 launch window.
The owner of Exophase blamed this leak on Steam owner Valve. “Seems like a possible screw up on Valve's end, a bunch of games with achievements that should be private are accessible through the API right now and that's why they got scanned into the site,” x3sphere said in a post on ResetEra. “I usually never see games without an actual name pop up with achievements, yet over the past hour or so a bunch have (when there's an unknown name we just set it to the AppID).”
Also included in the leak are a number of unannounced games, such as a Steam release for Capcom’s much-loved Nintendo 3DS game, Professor Layton vs. Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney. There’s also an unannounced Nickelodeon game, unannounced Telltale Games The Walking Dead Collection, and an unannounced Tetris game. Gematsu has a roundup.
Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: IGN Australia and Chupa Chups to Host a Retro Gaming ‘Fun House’ Activation at Westfield Parramatta This October
item.description:
Looking for some free fun October 1 to 4? Chupa Chups is teaming up with IGN Australia and Westfield Parramatta for four days of free gaming goodness this October school holidays.
We're calling it the “Chupa Chups Forever Fun House” - and Aussie IGNers are invited to come check out our 90s family dream home: four decorated rooms, loads of consoles and games, free Chupa Chups lollies and daily prize giveaways!
Doors open as soon as Westfield does - and it lasts all day until close, so come along and check it out. Did we mention it’s free?
So what’s on show? We’ll have instant multiplayer party-makers like Mario Kart World, Super Smash Bros Ultimate and Minecraft Dungeons II.

item.title: Netflix is adapting Larry McMurtry’s iconic Western novel Lonesome Dove into a new TV series from East of Eden co-showrunners Zoe Kazan and Jeb Stuart.
item.description:
Netflix has ordered a series retelling of Larry McMurtry's Pulitzer Prize-winning Western novel Lonesome Dove.
The project will reteam the streaming service with East of Eden co-showrunners Zoe Kazan and Jeb Stuart. Teton Ridge Entertainment owns the film and TV rights to McMurtry's Lonesome Dove book series.
McMurtry's 1985 bestseller follows former Texas Rangers-turned-cowboys Augustus "Gus" McRae and Woodrow Call, who embark on a fateful 3,000-mile cattle drive to Montana, encountering a variety of frontier dangers along the way.
CBS adapted it as a blockbuster TV miniseries in 1989 starring Robert Duvall, Tommy Lee Jones, Danny Glover, Rick Schroder, Diane Lane, Robert Urich, Anjelica Huston, Steve Buscemi, Chris Cooper, Frederic Forrest, and Glenne Headly.
“After our singular experience on East of Eden, we are thrilled to be teaming with Netflix again, along with Teton Ridge Entertainment, to bring Larry McMurtry’s western classic to life,” Kazan and Stuart said in a statement (via Deadline).
“We come to this material with love and respect, and can’t wait to hit the trail with Gus and Call and the rest of these beloved characters. Yee-haw.”
According to Deadline, Kazan and Stuart will executive produce Lonesome Dove with Thomas Tull, Jillian Share and Jen Gorton of Teton Ridge Entertainment; Jon Jashni; late McMurtry’s longtime creative partner Diana Ossana; Curtis McMurtry of the McMurtry Estate.
when we'd be standing around on set of EAST OF EDEN, waiting for the next set-up, my friend/co-showrunner (and screenwriter of THE FUGITIVE and DIE HARD) Jeb Stuart would talk my ear off about how I had to read Larry McMurtry. i finally listened to him--and now... https://t.co/9XyaPDTx7m
Other books in McMurtry’s Lonesome Dove literary series include Streets of Laredo (1993), Dead Man's Walk (1995), and Comanche Moon (1997), all of which were also adapted for television. There was also Lonesome Dove: The Series, which ran for two seasons in syndication in the 1990s.
Kazan and Stuart’s East of Eden launches on Netflix on October 1. It stars Florence Pugh, Christopher Abbott, Mike Faist, Hoon Lee, Joseph Zada, and Joe Anders.

item.title: The 2026 Rocket League World Championship Finals will be broadcast at 50 AMC Theaters across the United States.
item.description:
The 2026 Rocket League World Championship Finals will be broadcast at 50 AMC Theaters across the United States.
The Finals take place on Sunday, September 20. That day, fans can show up to participating AMC Theaters nationwide and catch the action on the big screen.
The competition will stream live from Dickies Arena in Fort Worth, Texas, where 20 teams will throw down for the chance to win $300,000 out of a staggering $1.2 million prize pool. The total broadcast will last approximately eight hours.
Tickets are currently on sale at participating theaters, with adult tickets priced at $19.49 ($22.18 if booked online). Only a few of these theaters are showing the Finals, and tickets are selling out fast, so make sure to grab yours quickly if you want a front row seat to see who gets crowned the 15th Rocket League World Champions.
Most major esports tournaments are streamed on Twitch, with viewers receiving special drops that can be earned by simply watching on the platform. AMC Theaters has already thought of this, and is giving fans commemorative Rocket League tickets that include codes to redeem the drops that they would normally get watching the competition on Twitch.
“Such a big part of the magic of movie theatres is their ability to bring people together for unforgettable shared experiences, and a live event like the Rocket League World Championship is a great example of that," Ellen Copaken, SVP of Business Development for AMC Theatres, said in a press release. "We're excited to give fans the opportunity to watch esports' biggest stage unfold live on massive screens, surrounded by fellow Rocket League fans.”
A full list of the participating theaters can be found at the link embedded here.
This isn’t the first time an esports tournament has been shown at a theater; last year, the League of Legends Worlds Finals in Chengdu, China were shown in select theaters across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. Riot did the same for the Valorant Champions Paris Finals, which also screened in certain cinemas throughout EMEA.
AMC’s decision to broadcast esports is the latest unique move from the brand after it founded a film distribution company to help get smaller films into theaters. With small-budget projects like Obsession and Markiplier’s Iron Lung proving to be hits at the box office, AMC is stepping in to capitalize on the trend and bring art to the masses.

item.title: The Rings of Power is finally getting a 4K Blu-ray release ahead of the Prime Video show's third season.
item.description:
The Rings of Power is finally getting a 4K Blu-ray release.
The Prime Video series inspired by J.R.R. Tolkien’s The Lord of The Rings has been a streaming exclusive since it first premiered back in 2022. Now, Amazon has revealed a spread of 4K Blu-ray releases for both seasons of the show, including some particularly gorgeous limited-edition steelbooks.
All of the DVD releases are now available to preorder ahead of their release dates in November and December, which will roughly coincide with the release of the show’s third season.
Both seasons of The Rings of Power are getting the same general breakdown of DVD releases. Your options, listed in order from the cheapest to the most expensive, are a standard DVD ($39.99), Blu-ray ($46.99), and 4K ($51.99), as well as Amazon-exclusive limited-edition 4K steelbooks ($61.99). The standard DVDs for both seasons will all be released on November 3, while the limited-edition steelbooks won’t ship until December 1.
The standard DVDs for Season 1 all feature the same cover art. You get a look at most of the main cast, though the focus is on Galadriel against the bright white background.
The 4K steelbook for this one has some fantastic old-school fantasy vibes, coming in a gold slipcase with frames images of Galadriel on the front and the Great Tree on the back. The steelbook also comes with six collectible art cards, each featuring some ethereal photographed portraits of individual characters.
Season 1 Bonus Features
Read IGN’s Full Review of The Rings of Power Season 1
The Season 2 Blu-ray cover art takes the spotlight away from Galadriel and instead points it almost toward Sauron. It also goes with the black background, having generally “darker” vibes than its first season companion.
Along similar lines, the 4K steelbook for Season 2 swaps out the gold slipcase for black, and the small image of Galadriel for a darker still of Sauron. The back of the slipcase shows off a forge. The full steelbook also comes with six more collectible art cards, this time featuring particularly action-packed and rugged poses.
Season 2 Bonus Features
Read IGN’s Full Review of The Rings of Power Season 2
The Rings of Power is returning for its third season on November 11, 2026. Because it’s been so long since Season 2, Prime Video has already confirmed the new season will kick off with a “Fellowship-style" prologue before diving into some tense battles and introducing new characters. While the show will once again stream exclusively on Prime Video, it will presumably get its own 4K Blu-ray release at some point in the future.

item.title: Neon has unveiled the first teaser for Luca Guadagnino's Sam Altman biopic, Artificial, after Amazon abruptly canceled its support for the film earlier this year.
item.description:
Neon has unveiled the first teaser for Luca Guadagnino's Sam Altman biopic, Artificial, after Amazon abruptly canceled its support for the film earlier this year.
With the director behind Challengers at the helm and a star-studded cast, the first teaser for the OpenAI movie somehow manages to surprise. In a little more than a minute, the trailer promises a tense look into Altman's life that leans heavily on the horror vibes, with the video teasing a peek behind the curtain into the events that led to the creation of controversial tech tool ChatGPT.
Altman, played by Andrew Garfield (The Social Network, The Amazing Spider-Man), can be seen walking through dark corridors backed by eerie strings before reaching a blue-lit room loaded with guns. It looks like the kind of saferoom the OpenAI CEO teased he might have when speaking to The New Yorker in 2016, but the horror elements come from more than the visuals. His character can be heard whispering lines, including "We opened Pandora's box together" and "We get to be the ones to shepherd people into this new world."
Garfield walks, talks, acts, and even looks like Altman in the first trailer for Artificial, but he's far from alone. Monica Barbaro (A Complete Unknown, Top Gun: Maverick) also shows up in the movie and its first teaser trailer as former OpenAI executive Mira Murati.
Cooper Hoffman (The Long Walk), Yura Borisov (Anora), Jason Schwartzman (Scott Pilgrim vs. the World), Mark Rylance (Bridge of Spies), and Chris O'Dowd (Bridesmaids) also have their own roles to play in Guadagnino's retelling. The role many viewers are likely already keeping an eye out for, though, is Ike Barinholtz's (The Studio) Elon Musk. Quick flashes of the Tesla boss do appear in the trailer, but they do little to tell watchers what to expect from his portrayal in Artificial.
Despite the star power and talent behind it, Artificial very nearly never came to be. Amazon was previously attached to release the project but chose to cut its involvement in June 2026, just three months ago. The move allegedly came just after multiple private test screenings for the nearly complete movie, leading to confusion amongst fans of Guadagnino's work. Amazon's decision to drop Artificial also happened to arrive only a few months after the company committed to a $50 billion investment in OpenAI.
Artificial was dropped by Amazon and eventually picked back up by Neon. It's now set to come to select theaters Christmas Day 2026. For more on OpenAI, you can read about how the tech company shut down its generative AI app Sora earlier this year.

item.title: Benjamin Burnley, lead singer and guitarist of the rock band Breaking Benjamin, took five minutes during a concert in Holmdel, New Jersey, to rant about his feud with a fellow Fallout 4 modder.
item.description:
Benjamin Burnley, lead singer and guitarist of the rock band Breaking Benjamin, took five minutes during a concert in Holmdel, New Jersey, to rant about his feud with a fellow Fallout 4 modder.
If you didn’t know Benjamin Burnley was a big gamer, now you do. He announced this information during a concert on Sunday, September 6, revealing that he’s an “amateur modder” for Skyrim and Fallout 4.
Lately, he’s been beefing with a fellow modder over a mod he recently created for Fallout 4 that allows users to play the game in first-person. He thinks it’s a pretty solid mod — but the other guy just doesn’t see the vision.
His spiel was caught on video by a fan at the concert, who posted footage of the moment on Reddit under the name ‘im_all_ears.’
“I just made a mod that makes it so that when you’re in first-person, you stay in first-person. You see your body in first-person. You go to your workshop area in first-person, and third-person still works. So, I want you to go and download that f**kin’ mod,” Burnley began.
“More importantly, I wanna tell you why I’m doing this. There was a modder — so, there’s like a clique, there was a modder in the community that was really mean to me and bullying me and saying, ‘Oh, you mod is sh*t, you don’t know what you’re f**kin’ doing, so I'm doing this every fucking night, and blowing his fucking downloads out of the water. Please help me destroy this f**kin’ jerk. I’m not even gonna say his name, but he’s a d**k, and f**k him.”
Production even posted the name of the mod on the venue’s big screen, along with Burnley's Nexus Mods username: “True First Person Mod by killemloud.”
“Even if you don’t play that game, go download it. It’s on Nexus Mods,” he urged. “And tomorrow, I better see all those downloads going up. …This is for people who love mods. I’m uploading the update for it. You know, when you post a mod, you’re supposed to be able to grow and learn, and make it better. And right off the bat, this f**kin’ a**hole was s**tin’ on my mod, and he ain’t lettin’ me update it. So that’s what happened.”
While there were quite a few gamers in the crowd who couldn’t get enough of this humorous feud, one or two vocal fans yelled at Burnley to “play some music” rather than rant about Update 1.2 for his first-person mod. The entire spiel took nearly five minutes, and it has since gone viral across social media for the reasons you might expect.
“No way Ben makes Fallout 4 mods, that's insane lol,” one wrote on Reddit.
“Benjamin Burnley makes gaming mods?! The f**k? That’s awesome!” another said.
Breaking Benjamin was also famously featured in Halo 2, but there’s oodles of celebrity gamers out there; most recently, Obsession star Inde Navarrette went viral for having a Twitch channel, where she streamed games in the Call of Duty series and story-based titles like The Last of Us, while Samara Weaving — recently cast as Emma Frost in Marvel’s upcoming X-Men movie — received praise for being such a hardcore gamer that she takes her PlayStation 5 with her on the road while she’s filming movies.

item.title: Snoop Dogg's biopic has cast Swayvo Twain, the son of D'Angelo, as Notorious B.I.G.
item.description:
Snoop Dogg's biopic has cast Swayvo Twain, the son of D'Angelo, as The Notorious B.I.G.
The Snoop Dogg biopic, simply titled Snoop, was announced in 2022, and is now ramping up for release next summer. Over the last couple of months, the film has added a number of actors to its cast to play legendary rappers like the titular musician himself, Nate Dogg, Dr. Dre, Tupac, and more. The movie is comprised of a mostly unknown/up-and-coming cast, which now includes Swayvo Twain, the son of D'Angelo.
Swayvo Twain will play one of the all-time great hip-hop artists, The Notorious B.I.G., in the film. It's unclear how much screen time he'll have in the actual movie itself, but he obviously played a big role in the rise of rap in the '90s. Snoop Dogg and Notorious B.I.G. were heavily involved in the East-Coast-West-Coast rivalry, which will almost certainly play a role in the movie. The film is being directed by Craig Brewer, who helmed 2025's Song Sung Blue and 2005's Hustle and Flow.
Snoop Dogg himself is having a pretty active time in the entertainment industry as a whole. The rapper is the current elusive target in Hitman and will play an original character in the Yakuza prequel, Stranger Than Heaven, next year. Tupac's likeness is also being leveraged for a different character in that title.

item.title: PlayStation architect Mark Cerny says he's "nearing the end" of his career and wants to pay it forward before he steps away, so he's partnered with The Game Awards creator Geoff Keighley to announce a new fellowship program for game design graduates called the The Nova Games Foundation, with a goal of awarding 20 graduates per year a six-figure grant.
item.description:
PlayStation architect Mark Cerny says he's "nearing the end" of his career and wants to pay it forward before he steps away, so he's partnered with The Game Awards creator Geoff Keighley to announce a new fellowship program for game design graduates called the The Nova Games Foundation, with a goal of awarding 20 graduates per year a six-figure grant.
Cerny and Keighley spoke to Game File to reveal the nonprofit program, which aims to run for decades, not just years, and promises mentorship to fellowship recipients in addition to the "no-strings" $100,000 grants. The beneficiaries of these awards can earn up to an additional half-million dollars "for projects that are shaping up particularly well." Those determinations will be made based on achieving development milestones.
“I’m nearing the end of my career,” Cerny told Game File's Stephen Totilo. “I’m not done yet, but paying it forward—in the best way possible—is very much on my mind these days.” Keighley added, “I’ve always wanted to give back, but given my role in the industry, I’ve never felt it appropriate to commercially invest in games. I’ve never owned stock in a game company or taken a financial stake in a game. Nova is philanthropy: we aren’t taking equity or looking to recoup the grants. The return we’re hoping for is creative—helping new voices make games and find their footing.”
Hazelight founder and game director on hit two-player co-op games A Way Out (which we loved), It Takes Two (we adored that one too), and Split Fiction (yup, you guessed it: we think it rocks) Josef Fares has already indicated his participation via donation and mentorship. Meanwhile, NYU and USC are two of 13 universities from around the world that will be part of the program. The first recipients will be from the classes of 2026 and 2027 from these universities, and they can begin applying in December of this year.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: Akira Nishitani, one of the original designers for Street Fighter 2 and Final Fight, expressed an interest in rebalancing Super Street Fighter 2: Turbo — over 30 years after its release.
item.description:
Akira Nishitani, one of the original designers for Street Fighter 2 and Final Fight, expressed an interest in rebalancing Super Street Fighter 2: Turbo — over 30 years after its release.
In September 2026 — 32 years after Super Turbo hit arcades in 1994 — Akira Nishitani, a legend in the fighting game world and a veteran of the industry, shared a post on X/Twitter with the wild concept of rebalancing the game after so many years.
“Is it okay to tweak [Super Street Fighter 2 Turbo] again?” he wrote, as spotted and translated by EventHubs. “I wasn't really involved much, but if it's possible, I'd kinda like to give it a shot. Sorry if it turns into a nerf fest, lol.”
スパⅡXを再調整するのアリですか？私はほとんど関わっていなかったのですが、もし可能ならやってみたいなぁ。ナーフ祭りになったらすみませんw
While Capcom has re-released a slew of its older fighting games over the years for various retro collections, we can’t imagine we’d get a totally rebalanced version of the original SSF2T, one of the most iconic titles in the Street Fighter 2 series. That being said, Nishitani himself believes that it deserves a second pass, though some members of the fighting game community aren’t so sure they agree with him.
For instance, James Chen, a longtime fighting game commentator and fighting game community (FGC) historian, believes such changes wouldn’t be well-received by players, given how beloved the title is and how fondly it's remembered.
“It’s dangerous, as so many love Super Turbo as it is. Many logical changes would be bad, to be honest. Removing, for example, Chun’s ability to store her Super would make her less interesting, while removing Honda’s stored Oicho Throw makes him more interesting (to fight, that is),” he explained.
“SSF2X, despite all the unbalanced stuff, is still a pretty loved game with a pretty active scene despite being +30 years old, so even if you want to balance it, you should be pretty careful with what to change,” another player warned.
It’s also worth noting that Nishitani no longer works at Capcom; he founded his own game development company, Arika, in 1995, where he continues to make games to this day. Fighting game fans might know the studio best for Fighting EX Layer, a spiritual successor to the Street Fighter EX series of the mid-90s.
Capcom has pulled off a few new spins on Super Street Fighter 2 Turbo over the years; in 2008, the company released Super Street Fighter 2 Turbo HD Remix, which was well-received by critics at the time. And in 2017, it released Ultra Street Fighter 2 for the Nintendo Switch, a remixed version of the game with updated graphics, additional characters, and balance changes — but with the current success of Street Fighter 6, it’s anyone’s guess as to whether or not Capcom is interested in overhauling its original older games once again.

item.title: The Trump Administration appears to have pulled its Tetris clone 'Build the Wall' offline less than one week after its launch.
item.description:
The Trump Administration appears to have pulled its 'Build the Wall' Tetris clone offline less than one week after its launch.
The title launched last week alongside a small collection of other games as part of yet another attempt from The White House to connect with U.S. gamers. Build the Wall has now vanished from the Arcade.Gov website (as spotted by VGC), while the four other games it launched alongside it remain.
Those who did try Build the Wall suggested it was clearly aimed to offend, not entertain. Aside from the criticism it received for its subject matter, which asked players to "protect the border from the incoming horde," players quickly realized the game itself didn't seem to be winnable at all. Instead of clearing filled lines, blocks would only continue to fall into place until reaching an inevitable ‘game over’ message when the screen was filled.
We don't know why the Tetris clone has disappeared, but we do know what followed after the Trump Administration launched Arcade.Gov. The website, which was marketed on social media with references to other gaming companies like Nintendo and Sega, quickly resulted in backlash online. The noise grew so loud so quickly that it didn't take long for The Tetris Company to respond.
"At Tetris, we believe in the power of connection and bringing people together, not dividing them," it said. "To our fans everywhere: we love you, we see you, and we're grateful to have you in our community."
P.S. The Tetris Company was not involved in the creation of ‘Build the Wall’.P.P.S. We take copyright infringement very seriously. pic.twitter.com/Fu02khRpT3
Although The Tetris Company also said it takes "copyright infringement very seriously," it did not detail any specific plans to take action against Build the Wall. It elaborated on its feelings in a statement sent to The Verge at the time.
"For more than 40 years, Tetris has brought people together across generations and cultures through play and joy," it told the site. "The objective of the game has always been to stack with purpose to clear as many lines as possible. We are currently reviewing the matter."
The Tetris Company had no comment to share.

item.title: Call of Duty's upcoming Halloween event will add the Doom Slayer as a playable operator to the game.
item.description:
Call of Duty's upcoming Halloween event will add the Doom Slayer to the game as a playable operator.
As part of what is expected to be the final season of content for Call of Duty: Black Ops 7, Activision is adding in one of the most iconic protagonists in FPS history: the Doom Slayer. The character will be added as part of The Haunting update, which will be released on September 17. Players will be able to acquire the Doom Slayer operator, inspired by Doom: The Dark Ages, as well as a Doomguy skin which is more in line with the character's look from the original Doom games. Of course, this will all be rounded out with signature Doom weaponry, including the shotgun, crucible blade, and the almighty BFG.
The legendary FPS icon will be added on September 24 via an event pass, which players can purchase. There will also be a free tier which will include various items, such as Doom-inspired skins like a UAC scientist and reseracher, weapon charms, and more. The premium tier will have the Doom Slayer operator skin and the more sought after weapon blueprints.
The Haunting update will include a variety of other non-Doom content, including a nighttime version of the Avalon map, spooky content and foes in Black Ops 7's Endgame mode, limited-time multiplayer modes, and new maps. It's one last hoorah for Black Ops 7 ahead of Modern Warfare 4's release in October, so be sure to hop in and check it out while it lasts.
Black Ops 7 is one of the lesser-recieved Call of Duty games, having launched with a poor campaign and a multiplayer mode that yielded mixed results from the community. The title was partially overshadowed by strong competition such as Battlefield 6 and Arc Radiers, but Treyarch has done its best to support the game with a steady stream of content and updated the game to implement player feedback. The open comms have also rubbed off on Infinity Ward, which has led to Modern Warfare 4 being fine tuned with the community in mind.

item.title: Nintendo has confirmed it intentionally included loading screens in its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake to "preserve the essence of the original game," and the internet isn't in love with the idea.
item.description:
Nintendo has confirmed that it intentionally included loading screens in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake to "preserve the essence of the original game," and the internet isn't in love with the idea.
Confirmation that loading screens would cut into the remake's playtime arrived during a gameplay demonstration shown as part of today's The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct. It's an extremely brief moment that saw series producer Eiji Aonuma confirm that the Ocarina of Time remake will channel the power of the Nintendo 64 when it launches for Nintendo Switch 2 this November.
"By the way, there's a loading screen whenever you move between areas," Aonuma said as Link and Navi traveled from Kokiri Forest to Hyrule Field. "This is something we intentionally kept to preserve the essence of the original game."
Let's take a second to break down the footage. In the 1998 Ocarina of Time, as well as so many other games before and after it, loading screens allowed developers to pause the experience and load new areas for the player to explore. With the exception of some cutscenes before and after the original transition between Kokiri Forest and Hyrule Field, players really only had control of Link taken away for a few seconds.
The Ocarina of Time remake appears to be a bit more seamless. It's unclear if Aonuma's demo will play out the same as the full release, but here, we see the player in control of Link before a black screen consumes the visuals. It and a small Triforce logo in the bottom right corner are on-screen for about three seconds before Young Link trots back into view.
Massive changes to the art style aside, Nintendo's decision to "preserve the essence" of 1998's groundbreaking adventure game seems to mostly line up. That said, in the nearly 30 years since that game came out, players have adapted to an advancing industry that often attempts to hide its loading screens – and that's if a game has them, at all.
Nintendo intentionally left some loading screen sections in the Ocarina of Time Remake to preserve the feel of the OG. pic.twitter.com/JBRtLfitq4
Choosing to intentionally include loading screens in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has players split. While some love the idea of a reimagining that pays homage to '90s N64 gaming, others see the breaks between gameplay as not only a silly addition but a confusing one, too. Some even suspect Nintendo included the loading screens because it needed them on the Switch 2, and not because it wanted them.
"Loading times in to preserve feel?" one fan said. "Lol I don't believe that for a second. It's fine that they are in there but don't say that's why you did it, Nintendo."
"'Loading times/screen still in the game between areas, added intentional to preserve feel of the game,' I'm sorry, what? Lmao," one fan said. "That's stupid."
"I didn’t mind that," another argued. "It makes the areas feel more apart and contrasted. That and also the loading screens are two seconds, so who gives a s**t."
pic.twitter.com/jmljZyfW1U
“The loading screen is intentional to keep the nostalgia of the original game” Legend of Zelda direct making me laugh pic.twitter.com/9yKxMKNZav
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches for Switch 2 November 5, 2026. It'll have more than redone load screens when it arrives, with players also still coming to grips with the wild changes Nintendo made to the game's visuals.
